title: Unique Paths
summary: Count paths from the top-left to the bottom-right of an m×n grid moving only right or down. Each cell is reached from above or from the left, so `dp[r][c] = dp[r−1][c] + dp[r][c−1]`. The first row and column have exactly one path each.

complexity.note: One row of size n is enough if you overwrite in place.

intuition: Every path into (r, c) comes from (r−1, c) or (r, c−1).
Border cells can only be reached in one way.
The closed form C(m+n−2, m−1) also works, but watch for overflow.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
summary: Find the length of the longest sequence that appears in both strings in order (not necessarily contiguous). `dp[i][j]` is the LCS of the first i and first j characters. Matching characters extend the diagonal; otherwise take the better of dropping one character from either string.

complexity.note: Can be reduced to O(min(m, n)) with two rows.

intuition: If `a[i−1] == b[j−1]`, that character is part of the LCS: `dp[i−1][j−1] + 1`.
Otherwise one of the two last characters isn't used: `max(dp[i−1][j], dp[i][j−1])`.
Row 0 and column 0 are empty prefixes: 0.
pitfalls: Off-by-one between dp indices and string indices.

title: Target Sum
summary: Assign + or − to every number so the total equals `target`; count the ways. If P is the sum of the + numbers, then `P − (total − P) = target`, so `P = (total + target) / 2`. Count subsets with that sum.
intuition: Rewriting the signs as a subset sum turns it into a counting knapsack.
If `total + target` is odd or `|target| > total`, the answer is 0.
Iterate sums downward so each number is used once.
Zeros double the count (±0 are different assignments); the DP handles that.
pitfalls: Forgetting the parity and range checks.
Negative target: use `abs(target)` in the range check.

title: Edit Distance
summary: Minimum inserts, deletes and replacements to turn `word1` into `word2`. `dp[i][j]` = cost for the first i and j characters. Equal characters cost nothing extra (diagonal); otherwise 1 + the best of replace (diagonal), delete (up) or insert (left).

complexity.note: Two rows are enough for the length only.

intuition: Row 0: building `word2[0..j)` from nothing takes j inserts. Column 0: i deletes.
Match: `dp[i][j] = dp[i−1][j−1]`.
Otherwise `1 + min(replace, delete, insert)`.
pitfalls: Mixing up which neighbour means insert vs delete (they're symmetric, so the answer survives, but the explanation doesn't).
Forgetting the base row and column.

title: Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock with Cooldown
summary: Trade as often as you like, but after selling you must wait a day. Track three states each day: `hold` (own a share), `sold` (just sold today), `rest` (no share, free to buy). Each state's best value comes from yesterday's states.
intuition: hold = max(hold, rest − price): keep holding, or buy today from a rested state.
sold = hold + price: sell what you held.
rest = max(rest, sold): yesterday's sale forces today's rest.
Answer: max(sold, rest); you never end holding.
pitfalls: Updating states in place without saving yesterday's values.
